questions.question: For a maximization LP with optimal value $z^*$, the shadow price $y_i^*$ of resource constraint $i$ with right-hand side $b_i$ is defined as which quantity?
options: The market price per unit of resource $i$
The amount of resource $i$ left unused at the optimum
How fast $z^*$ changes as $b_i$ rises slightly
The change in $z^*$ when constraint $i$ is removed

questions.question: For a maximization LP with $\le$ resource constraints and slack variables $s_i$, the final simplex tableau is written as $z+\sum_jq_jx_j=z_0$, over all variables. Where can the shadow price of resource $i$ be read?
options: The right-hand side of the row where $s_i$ is basic
The objective-row coefficient of $x_i$, the $i$-th product
The right-hand side $z_0$ of the objective row
The objective-row coefficient of the slack $s_i$

questions.question: At the optimum of a maximization LP, the $\le$ constraint for resource $i$ has slack $s_i=12>0$, so 12 units of the resource are unused. What is its shadow price?
options: 12, the number of units left unused
Negative, as unused units are wasted
0, as extra unused units add nothing
Positive, as more resource is always useful

questions.question: At the optimum of a maximization LP, machine time has shadow price 4 (profit per extra hour) for small changes. A supplier offers extra hours at a price $p$ per hour, not yet included in the model. When do a few extra hours raise net profit?
options: When $p>4$, since dearer hours are more valuable
Always, as machine time has a positive shadow price
Never, as the LP optimum already uses all hours well
When $p<4$, since each hour adds 4 and costs $p$

questions.question: A maximization LP has optimal value 45, and the shadow price of its labour constraint is 2.5 per hour. Four labour hours are lost, and the current basis stays optimal. What is the new optimal value?

A maximization LP with $\le$ constraints and slacks $s_1,s_2,s_3$ has final objective row $z+\tfrac{7}{5}s_1+\tfrac{1}{5}s_2=17$, with $x_1$, $x_2$, $s_3$ basic. What are the shadow prices of resources 1, 2 and 3?
options: $\tfrac{5}{7}$, 5 and 0

questions.question: A maximization LP measures profit in euros, and one constraint limits flour used, in kilograms, to $b$ kg. Its shadow price is 2. In which unit is the number 2 expressed, and what does it mean?
options: Kg per euro: 2 kg more flour per euro earned
Euros per kg: one more kg adds about 2 euros
Euros: the flour costs 2 euros in total
Kg: 2 kg of flour remain unused

questions.question: Why is the shadow price of a $\le$ resource constraint in a maximization LP never negative?
options: More resource enlarges the feasible set, so the optimum cannot fall.
Shadow prices are defined as absolute values of slack coefficients.
Resources always have a positive market price.
The simplex method only stops at nonnegative values.

questions.question: A maximization LP contains a minimum-requirement constraint $x_2\ge b$, such as a contracted delivery. If $b$ is raised slightly, in which direction can the optimal value move?
options: Only up, as for every resource constraint.
Only up, since $x_2$ adds profit.
Either way, depending on the objective.
Down or not at all, as plans are removed.

questions.question: At the optimum of a maximization LP with $\le$ resource constraints, consider the statements P: the shadow price of resource $i$ is positive, and Q: constraint $i$ is binding (zero slack). Which relation holds?
options: Q implies P, but not the other way round.
P and Q are equivalent.
P implies Q; the converse fails.
Neither implies the other.

questions.question: For a maximization LP, re-solving with resource level $b=40$ gives optimal value 260 and with $b=44$ gives 270, with the same optimal basis throughout. What is the shadow price of this resource?

For: maximize $3x_1+2x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\le4$, $2x_1+x_2\le6$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$, the optimum is $(2,2)$ with value 10 and both constraints bind. Raising the first right-hand side to 5 keeps both binding. What is the shadow price of the first constraint?

At the optimum of a maximization LP, a raw material constraint has slack 12 units, so its shadow price is 0. A buyer offers 2 per unit for 5 units of this material, which are removed from the right-hand side. How does total profit change?
options: It falls by 10: five units are sold.
It rises by 10: the plan still holds.
It is unchanged: shadow price 0.
It rises by 24: $12\cdot2$ for all.

questions.question: For a maximization LP with $\le$ constraints, the final objective row is $z+\sum_jq_jx_j+\sum_iy_is_i=z_0$. Why is the slack coefficient $y_i$ the rate of change of $z^*$ in $b_i$?
options: Raising $b_i$ by $\Delta$ acts like $s_i=-\Delta$, so $z=z_0+y_i\Delta$.
It is like adding $\Delta$ to $s_i$, so $z$ falls by $y_i\Delta$.
The slack's original objective coefficient is $y_i$, its resource price.
Every unit of $b_i$ is turned into one unit of slack $s_i$ at optimum.

questions.question: For: maximize $x_1$ subject to $x_1\le3$ (constraint 1), $x_2\le2$ (constraint 2), $x_1,x_2\ge0$, the simplex method returns the optimal point $(3,2)$, where both constraints bind. What is the shadow price of constraint 2?
options: 0, since $b_2$ has no effect on $z^*$
1, as constraint 2 binds at $(3,2)$
2, the right-hand side of constraint 2
Undefined, as the optimum is not unique

questions.question: A maximization LP's objective is revenue minus material cost, with material counted at 3 per kg used; the constraint 'kg used $\le b$' has shadow price 1.4. Extra kg can be ordered at a price $p$ per kg, which replaces the cost 3 for those kg. Up to which $p$ do a few extra kg pay?
options: $p<1.4$, the shadow price itself
$p<4.4$, as 3 per kg is already charged
$p<3$, the cost already in the model
$p<1.6$, the cost 3 minus the shadow price

questions.question: For: maximize $3x_1+2x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\le6$ and a delivery requirement $x_2\ge2$, with $x_1,x_2\ge0$, the optimum is $(4,2)$ with value 16. What is the rate of change of the optimal value when the requirement 2 is raised slightly?
options: $-1$ per extra unit of requirement
$+2$, the profit of each extra $x_2$
$0$, as the requirement binds
$+1$, the size of the trade-off

questions.question: For a maximization LP, the shadow price of a resource is 2 at its current amount $b=50$. A planner predicts the optimal value at $b=500$ by adding $2\cdot450$. What is wrong with this prediction?
options: Shadow prices apply only to decreases of $b$, not to increases.
The rate 2 is guaranteed only within the RHS sensitivity range.
The rate must be applied to $b=500$ itself, not to $450$.
Shadow prices are valid for a change of exactly one unit.
